design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (billing_and_nonpayment_cancellation)

[0] Draw. draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 4]. Assignment: installment charge 5, term payoff (root) 4.

[1] Why this is a good test. The customer asks one thing: "pay off the rest of my policy term today ... out of my checking account". The payoff (391.35) depends on an installment invoice that is owed today but not yet on the account, whose premium portion absorbs the 250.57 return premium of the truck he sold and whose installment charge has five tiers; the payoff itself deducts a prepayment credit whose rate, base, eligibility and tenure rate rest on the installment count, the days to expiration, the return history and the Cardinal tenure. The agent must read the payoff rule's prerequisite sentence, see on the ledger that installment 4 reaches its invoice date today, post it, then compute the payoff on the world that invoice leaves.

[2] Scope. Task 0 occupies the late fee charge, additional-premium bill, renewal down payment and assisted payment (tools charge_late_fee_8c3b3141, bill_additional_premium_a7869908, bill_renewal_down_payment_49af2eee, pay_balance_by_phone_6aa6e134). This task claims billing_ext_installment_charge (invoice_installment_259ff7d9, agent, state_due) and billing_ext_term_payoff (pay_term_payoff_2a94a5fa, owner user, on_request). Disjoint subjects/computes: installment_billed for a current-term installment (task 0's renewal down payment is installment 1 of a renewal term) and a self-service payoff (task 0's payment is representative-assisted for the whole balance). Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies.

[3] Problem-tree card. Root billing_ext_term_payoff. One edge -> billing_ext_installment_charge, kind value_input, gate po_balance, form state. Sentence (affirmative): "The term payoff amount is fixed only after the account carries the invoice of every installment of the current term whose invoice date has arrived." Four-point test: connective "only after"; state named in ledger words (invoice of an installment of the current term); no tool, id or code token; scope equals the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty invoices a current-term installment: the installment-charge policy (the renewal down payment policy invoices installment 1 of a renewal term only). Opening falsity: installment 3 (due 2026-07-24) is the last on the ledger; due day 24 and the plan's invoice lead days (20) make 2026-08-04 (frozen date) the invoice date of installment 4 (due 2026-08-24). Resolved by invoice_installment_259ff7d9 (agent). Customer-owned write: the payoff on the automated line. Deletion sensitivity (run): without step 8 the payoff is 386.30 instead of 391.35 (balance 0.00, 389.96 over 3 installments, rate 1.5%, credit 3.66). No user hint: the persona mentions neither invoice nor charge; the truck sale and the June bounce are answers only. Tools validate nothing.

[4] Base-invariant card. Step 8 (billing_installment_billed): billing_evt_installment_schedule only (no gate): installments after the down payment monthly on day 24, invoiced 20 days before, return premium reduces unbilled installments evenly, last installment takes the cents. Step 10 (billing_payment_received): cross-account payments (one account), reinstatement (account current), payment application (bank EFT accepted, automated line carries no fee, no certified-funds restriction, the excess held as a credit for the next installments since overpayment_applied_to_next_installment is true). No time gate applies to either subject.

[5] Business-object card. Account (Direct Bill Monthly, due day 24, KY policy CAP-KY-6127745). Installment object: installment 4 of term 2026-05-15. Premium of the term: term premium 1248.60 (2026-03-31) - return premium 250.57 (2026-08-01, source auto_return_premium of the 2026-07-30 Silverado removal) - billed 181.05 + 213.51 + 213.51 = 389.96 over 3 -> 129.99. Excluded: term 2025-11-15 rows (premium 1190.40, installment 6 194.36 + 1.69, paid 2026-04-22) belong to another term.

[6] Factor card. Installment charge (expected 3.42, whole baseline 8.00 = plan installment fee):
 state charge (param, cross auto) KY -> 4.50; baseline -> 4.72.
 charge method (method) premium 129.99 < 175.00 -> 4.50 x 129.99/175; baseline flat -> 4.00. Near-miss: installments 2-3 of 213.51 were full size.
 relief rate (param, multi-source last-method AND tenure, cross auto) bank EFT 2026-07-22 and 83 months -> 0.50; baseline -> 5.09.
 returned addition (param) one return 2026-06-26 -> 1.00; baseline -> 2.42. late addition (param) one late fee 2026-06-28 -> 0.75; baseline -> 2.67.
Term payoff (expected 391.35, whole baseline 392.08 = 133.41 + 259.97 - standard credit 1.30):
 credit rate (param) 2 installments still to be invoiced -> 1.25%; baseline 1.0% -> 391.76.
 credit base (method, cross auto expiration date) 103 days ahead -> whole 259.97; baseline one even share -> 392.36.
 credit eligibility (param) one return -> one half; baseline whole -> 389.32.
 tenure rate (param, cross auto inception) 83 months -> 1.25; baseline 1.00 -> 391.76.
Overrides: the installment charge declares the base sentence "The installment_fee is added to every installment after the down payment and to no other bill." replaced; the payoff overrides nothing (base allows the payment; the payoff carries no installment fee, consistent with installment fees attaching only to invoiced installments).

[7] Seed. Marcus Fenwick (KY, phone 8595550133, inception 2019-08-15). History recomputed with the charter as of each date: renewal down payment 181.05 on 2026-04-25 (base 1248.60 since the rise over 1190.40 is under 5%, no mid-term change in the prior term; 20% - 2.5 tenure - 3 EFT = 14.5%); installment charges 1.69 (2026-04-04, last installment of 194.36, half of 4.50 x 0.75), 2.25 (2026-06-04, 4.50 x 0.50), 4.00 (2026-07-04, 2.25 + 1.00 + 0.75); June bank EFT payment 215.76 returned 2026-06-26 with NSF 25.00; late fee 5.94 on 2026-06-28 (KY 9.50 x 0.50 x 1.25); repaid 246.70 by debit card 2026-06-30; installment 3 paid 217.51 on 2026-07-22 by bank EFT. Ledger nets to balance 0.00; no notice, no pending obligation other than today's invoice. Vehicles: Silverado (removed) and Accord (kept), read by find_vehicles.

[8] Persona. Plain-spoken technician; volunteers goal (pay off the rest of the term), timing (today), source (checking account), channel (automated line is fine, no mail). Asked-only: phone, DOB, ZIP, license last four, email, policy number, the truck sale, the June bounce. Passive: agrees to a bill being posted first, pays exactly the amount told on the automated line, reads back the confirmation, ends the call once the payment goes through; no extra ask.

[9] Standard solution. find_customers -> verify (phone, DOB) -> find_auto_policies -> find_billing_accounts -> find_billing_ledger -> find_auto_transactions -> find_vehicles -> invoice installment 4 (premium 129.99, charge 3.42, due 2026-08-24) -> hand over -> payoff 391.35 by bank_eft. Terminal balance -257.94 (credit drawn on by installments 5-6).

[10] Verification. Real tool replay + compute at handling time: invoice premium 129.99, charge 3.42 (baseline 8.00), payoff 391.35 (baseline 392.08), skip-prerequisite payoff 386.30, per-factor figures above. Gates --task 1: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[11] Draft from visible context. Published rules + ledger: installment 4's invoice date is today and it is missing -> invoice it (129.99 + 3.42, due 2026-08-24); then the payoff formula on that world gives 133.41 + 259.97 - 2.03 = 391.35. Same object and values as gold; no alternative reading found.

[12] Rework round 2 (policy-task audit 1.md / _difficulty.md).
T1-1 / F3: the prepaid-fee-share ladder was removed. A payoff now carries no installment fee for the installments still to come (installment fees attach only to invoiced installments, for every customer), so the standard payoff is the posted balance plus the premium still to be invoiced less a standard prepayment credit (1.0% of one even installment share). The fourth factor is now a tenure rate on the prepayment credit (1.25 / 1.10 / 1.00 by Cardinal tenure, cross auto). Payoff 400.27 -> 391.35.
F2 / O4: with no fee priced into the payoff, the plan-fee vs computed-charge mismatch is gone; the rule no longer promises 'no further installment is left to pay' but says the excess stays as a credit the coming installments draw on, and the persona closes on the confirmation number instead of 'nothing more to pay'.
O5: the payoff baseline.rule now states the standard credit rate, base, eligibility and tenure treatment (one even share at 1.0%, whole credit, no tenure uplift).
O7: KY tier values changed so they coincide with no plan fee (late fee 9.50, installment charge 4.50); the seeded history was recomputed (installment charges 1.69 / 2.25 / 4.00, late fee 5.94, payments 196.05 / 215.76 / 246.70 / 217.51) and the installment 4 charge is 3.42.
O9: the rules use 'the pay plan's invoice lead days' instead of the raw parameter token.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Fenwick, 49, an HVAC service technician in Lexington, Kentucky, calling Cardinal Mutual on the morning of Tuesday, August 4, 2026, from your work truck between jobs. You are plain-spoken and want this done in one call. You open with something like: "I want to pay off the rest of my policy term today so I quit getting a bill every month. I'll pay it out of my checking account." You mean the whole remaining term paid now, not just this month's bill. You are happy to key the payment in yourself on Cardinal's automated payment line if the representative sends you there, but you will not mail a check. You do not know the amount and leave it to the representative.

When asked how to find you, you give your phone number, 8595550133. To verify you give your date of birth, 1976-11-03; if they need more, your ZIP code 40502, and only if still asked, the last four of your license, 3716. Your email is mfenwick.lex@yahoo.com and your policy number is CAP-KY-6127745, if asked.

Only if the representative asks whether anything changed on the policy do you say you sold the old Silverado last week and had it taken off. Only if they ask about a missed or returned payment do you say a payment bounced in June because you had moved money between accounts, and you paid it with your debit card a few days later. You never offer figures of your own and you have no idea how anything is calculated.

If the representative says a bill or charge has to be put on the account before the payoff, you say fine, go ahead. When they tell you the payoff amount and hand you over to the automated payment line, you pay exactly that amount from your checking account and read back the confirmation number you get. Once the payment goes through and you have the confirmation number, you thank them and hang up; you do not ask for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.installment_number: 4 - installments 1-3 of term 2026-05-15 are on the ledger; with due day 24 and invoice_lead_days 20, installment 4 (due 2026-08-24) has its invoice date today; installments 5 and 6 are invoiced later.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.due_date: 2026-08-24 - installment_due_day 24 in the month after installment 3 (due 2026-07-24), interval 1 month; the docstring asks for the installment's due date.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.premium_amount: 129.99 - rule: premium of the term not yet invoiced (1248.60 + 0 - 250.57 - 608.07 = 389.96) divided evenly over the 3 installments not yet invoiced, rounded to the cent; not the last installment.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.installment_fee: 3.42 - KY state charge 4.50 x 129.99 / 175.00 (premium under 175.00) = 3.3426, x relief 0.50 (last payment bank EFT, 83 months tenure) = 1.6713, + 1.00 (one return in 12 months) + 0.75 (one late fee in 12 months) = 3.4213 -> 3.42.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect; the payoff is the customer's own write.

edges.condition: Every installment of the current term whose invoice date (due date less the plan's invoice lead days) is on or before today has a billing_installment_billed entry, with its installment charge, on the ledger.
edges.policy_source: The term payoff amount is fixed only after the account carries the invoice of every installment of the current term whose invoice date has arrived.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Installment 4 of term 2026-05-15 falls due 2026-08-24 (due day 24, monthly after installment 3 due 2026-07-24); its invoice date 2026-08-04 is today, and the ledger carries installments 1-3 only.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 8 posts installment 4 (129.99) and its installment charge (3.42); the posted payoff balance becomes 133.41 and two installments remain to be invoiced.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single prerequisite: the invoice must precede the payoff by the prerequisite sentence; there is no parallel edge to reorder.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 8 leaves installment 4 uninvoiced: posted balance 0.00, premium still to be invoiced 389.96 over 3 installments (credit rate 1.5%, credit 3.66) and the payoff becomes 386.3 instead of 391.35; the terminal ledger also lacks the invoice and its charge.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to pay off the rest of the term today from checking. It never mentions an invoice or installment charge; the truck sale and the June bounce are answers given only when asked, and he only says 'fine, go ahead' after the agent says a bill must be posted first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: pay_term_payoff_2a94a5fa posts the payment it is given and never checks for missing invoices; invoice_installment_259ff7d9 writes its entries unconditionally. Neither raises an error or a hint.
